utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Ira, what exactly still needs fixing for the repair drive, and who’s already signed up to help?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: I’m not totally sure yet, Mina—I haven’t heard the full list while I’ve been out. I can ask around on my next errands and let you know who’s already signed up.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Good, please ask today if you can, and get the actual list of broken items plus names of helpers so we don’t double up.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Noah, I heard you’re getting the repair drive going—want me to bring my toolbox and a few spare extension cords?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, yeah, that’d be great—bring the toolbox and cords if you can. I think we’re fixing up a few things out front.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: You got it, I’ll bring the toolbox and the extension cords and swing by out front a little early to help set up.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, I heard the repair drive’s getting a good bit of support—people seem ready to pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: That’s encouraging, but I’m a little worried about the practical side—where we’ll sort the items, how we’ll track repairs, and who’s handling drop-offs.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’s exactly the sort of thing we should pin down early—I can ask around and see who’s got space, clipboards, or a spare afternoon for drop-offs.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Happy to help with the repair drive—what do you need me to do?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Sam—could you start by noting who’s bringing tools and where they’ll drop them off? I’m keeping a location list so nothing gets misplaced.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely—I’ll start a list of who’s bringing tools and where they’ll drop them off. Send me the names and locations, and I’ll keep it organized.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Uli, I’m glad I caught you—there’s a repair drive coming together, and I’m trying to make sure everyone hears about it fast.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Thanks for letting me know, Quinn. I’ll spread the word if I can.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Thanks, Uli — that’d help a lot. I’ll keep sharing the details so nobody misses the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Leo, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive — I’ve got the sign-up list ready. What should we prioritize first?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Let’s start with the biggest safety fixes first—loose steps, broken rails, and anything electrical. After that, we can work through the smaller stuff.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That sounds like the right order, Leo — I’ll mark safety fixes at the top of the list and ask folks to flag anything urgent when they sign up.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Hi Dane, before we jump in, can you tell me which repairs are most urgent and who has already offered help?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: I’m just catching up, Hana, so I don’t want to guess yet. Tell me what’s already been reported, and I’ll help sort out the urgent ones.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Of course — send me the reported repairs and I’ll sort the urgent ones first.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can help, but I need to work around school pickup times. What time is the repair drive happening?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Thanks, Faye — the repair drive is planned for Saturday from 10 to 2, so we can definitely work around pickup times.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: That works for me — I can cover the late morning shift, maybe 10 to noon, and still keep the afternoon free for family stuff.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Jules, I’m still catching up on the repair drive—have you heard what folks need most right now?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Mostly tools, a few spare hands, and someone to help sort what’s urgent. I can check around and see who still needs what.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That’d be really helpful, thanks. If you hear the biggest gaps, let me know and I can pass it along.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Yep, I can help, just give me the quick version of what you need.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Alright, Bo—just to confirm, you’re actually available to help with the repair drive, not just saying maybe?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Yeah, I’m available—just tell me where to show up and what time.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I can help with the repair drive. What do you need me to bring?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, thank you, Rey — I think we still need extension cords and a small toolkit, if you’ve got either handy.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I can bring two extension cords and a small toolkit. I’ll label them with my name so they don’t get mixed up.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Cleo, I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—do you know the plan yet? I can help spread the word once we’ve got the details.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’m still gathering the details, but I’m making a list of what supplies we’ll need and who can bring them. Once I’ve got the time and location confirmed, I’ll pass it along so you can help spread the word.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Perfect, Cleo—send me the time, location, and supply list when you’ve got them, and I’ll make sure the neighbors hear the plan.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Rey, I was just out picking up groceries and heard folks are starting to talk about the repair drive. What’s the latest on what still needs fixing?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I haven’t heard the full list yet, but I know they’re still gathering what needs fixing. If you hear anything specific, let me know.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Will do — I’ll keep my ears open while I’m out. If I hear any specific repair needs, I’ll pass them along.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh right, the repair drive—sorry, I blanked for a second. How can I help, Vik?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: No worries, Oren — we’re gathering broken small appliances at the community room Saturday morning, and I’m telling folks you can help sort and label things if that works.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Yes, that works for me—Saturday morning at the community room, sorting and labeling. I’ll write it down now so I don’t forget.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, right—the repair drive. I might’ve missed the details, what’s the plan again?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: We’re meeting at the hall tomorrow to drop off repair items, then sorting everything after lunch.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Got it, tomorrow at the hall for drop-off, then sorting after lunch. I’ll try to remember to bring the box of cords I’ve been meaning to fix.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Count me in for the repair drive — I can lend a few tools if you need them.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Thank you, Gus, that’s very helpful. Let’s make a simple list of what you can bring and set a drop-off time so nothing gets misplaced.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Sure thing — I can bring a cordless drill, socket set, screwdrivers, pliers, and a couple extension cords. I can drop them off Saturday morning around 9 if that works.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Hi Quinn, I’m glad we’re talking about the repair drive—what still needs sorting out?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hi Mara! I can start spreading the word right away—do we have a time, place, and list of items people should bring?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Thanks, Quinn—let’s say Saturday 10 to 2 at the community room, and folks can bring small appliances, lamps, bikes, and torn clothing, but no hazardous items.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Opal, I was thinking the repair drive could be a nice way to bring a few different circles together—do you already have a spot in mind for it?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I don’t have a firm spot yet, but I’m leaning toward somewhere central like the community room or the library annex. I can check availability and make a little list of pros and cons.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That sounds perfect—if you make the list, I can ask around and see which spot feels easiest for the different groups to get to.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Cleo, I’m glad we’re getting the repair drive moving—would you be willing to help me list what neighbors need fixed first?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Of course, Rosa—I can start a simple list and note who needs what fixed first. I’ll check with folks on our block and keep the supplies needed alongside each repair.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That would be wonderful, Cleo—thank you. If you can share the first few names and supply needs by Friday, I’ll start matching volunteers to each repair.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Mina, I’ve only heard bits and pieces about the repair drive—do you know what’s still needed?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: I’m not sure yet, Nell—what items have people already offered, and who’s keeping the list?

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I only heard second-hand that some tools and paint were already promised, but I don’t know who’s keeping the list. If you find out, could you let me know?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Faye, I’m a bit slammed today, but what’s the quick version on the repair drive—what do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Just need a quick headcount and a couple volunteers for pickup/drop-off windows. I’m trying to work it around school hours so it stays manageable.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—count me in for one, and I can probably do a pickup window after school if you send me the time.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Kira, I’d be happy to help with the repair drive—what do you need most right now?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: That’s kind of you, Sam, but can you confirm you’re actually free this Saturday and not just offering in passing?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Yes, I’m free this Saturday and I mean it—I can be there to help with the repair drive.
